subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Transform the equation x/a + y/b = 1 into normal form. If the perpendicular distance of the straight line from the Origin is p then deduce that 1/p² = 1/a² + 1/b².

mark_split.label: Read off cosα, sinα and p

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.64 — SAQ chapter 9 The Straight Line, answer 61. The original label came from the Baby Bullet-Q blueprint for the superseded 75-mark paper; the Sri Chaitanya FAST TRACK IPE Mathematics-IB 2026-27 edition files this chapter under the banner 8M + 2 × 2M = 12M, asks this question as Long Answer Question 15, and prints no short-answer block for it at all. Only the question was taken; the working, the mark split and every note here are ours (docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md). The question makes two separate demands, so the marks follow them: five for the transformation into normal form (clearing the fractions, the divide, and the term-by-term comparison that produces cosα, sinα and p) and three for the deduction that closes it. recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what you divide by to reach normal form, and what you do to p at the end.

steps.label: Clear the fractions
steps.margin_note: First mark. Normal form has no fractions, so the intercept form is cleared to ax + by = c shape before anything else.
lines: The given equation is  x/a + y/b = 1

recall.must_convey: That the intercept form is cleared to bx + ay = ab.
accept: clear the fractions to get b x plus a y equals a b
multiply through by a b
put it over a common denominator first
fractions clear chesi b x plus a y equals a b
remove the denominators

steps.why: Normal form is xcosα + ysinα = p, which has no denominators — so the fractions have to go first.
common_mistakes: Multiplying only one term by ab.
Writing ax + by = ab with a and b swapped.
steps.memory_tip: Normal form has NO fractions, so clear the intercept form to ax + by = c shape first.

steps.label: Divide by √(a²+b²)
steps.margin_note: The next two marks. Normal form needs the coefficients of x and y to square-and-add to 1, which is exactly what dividing by √(a²+b²) arranges.
lines: On dividing by √(a² + b²), we get

recall.must_convey: That both sides are divided by √(a² + b²).
accept: divide throughout by the root of a squared plus b squared
make the coefficients square and add to one
divide both sides by root a square plus b square
root a square plus b square tho divide cheyyali
this puts it into normal form
heard_as: root a squared plus b squared

steps.why: cos²α + sin²α = 1 forces this exact divisor — no other choice puts the equation into normal form.
common_mistakes: Dividing by a + b instead of √(a² + b²).
steps.memory_tip: Divide by √(a²+b²) so the x and y coefficients square-and-add to 1.

steps.label: Read off cosα, sinα and p
steps.margin_note: Two more marks. Compare with xcosα + ysinα = p term by term. Note that cosα takes b and sinα takes a — the letters cross over, because the x-intercept is a but the x-coefficient is b.
lines: This is in the normal form  xcosα + ysinα = p,  where
cosα = b/√(a²+b²),   sinα = a/√(a²+b²)   and   p = ab/√(a²+b²)

recall.must_convey: That comparing with xcosα + ysinα = p gives cosα = b/√(a²+b²), sinα = a/√(a²+b²) and p = ab/√(a²+b²).
accept: compare with x cos alpha plus y sin alpha equals p and read off each part
cos alpha is b over the root and sin alpha is a over the root
p is a b over root a squared plus b squared
normal form tho compare chesi read off cheyyali
the perpendicular distance p is a b over the root

steps.why: Only p is needed for the deduction, but the comparison has to be written out — the question asks for the normal form as well as the result.
common_mistakes: Assigning cosα = a/√(a²+b²), with a and b the wrong way round.
steps.memory_tip: The letters CROSS OVER: cos α takes b and sin α takes a, because the x-intercept is a but the x-coefficient is b.

steps.label: Deduce the result
steps.margin_note: The last three marks. Square p, invert it, and split the single fraction into two — the a² and b² separate because the numerator is a product.

recall.must_convey: That squaring and inverting p gives 1/p² = 1/a² + 1/b².
accept: square p then invert and split the fraction into two
one over p squared is a squared plus b squared over a squared b squared
split it as one over a squared plus one over b squared
p square chesi invert chesi split cheyyali
hence one by p squared equals one by a squared plus one by b squared

steps.why: Inverting is what turns the sum in the numerator into a sum of two separate fractions, which is the form the question asks for.
steps.memory_tip: Square p, invert, and split the fraction — a² and b² separate because the numerator is a product.
